Southwest Airlines’ compliance with the 737 MAX MCAS system has proceeded in three stages, each mandated by a U.S. FAA air-worthiness directive (AD) under 14 CFR Part 39.  

1. **Grounding and return-to-service (AD 2020-05-11)** - After the FAA Emergency Order of Airworthiness (March 13 2019) grounded all 737-8/9 aircraft, Southwest grounded its MAX fleet (first MAX 8 delivered August 29 2017). The airline complied with AD 2020-05-11, which required a series of inspections, software updates, and training before revenue service could resume. Southwest returned its MAX 8 fleet to service on March 11 2021, meeting the return-to-service requirements of that AD【714da224-4d04-46f9-ae7f-d85ca12a9df5】.  

2. **Enhanced AOA-sensor monitoring (AD 2022-03-07)** - The FAA issued AD 2022-03-07 to improve angle-of-attack (AOA) sensor monitoring and redundancy. Southwest implemented the required hardware and software changes to satisfy this directive, thereby ensuring continuous, reliable AOA data for MCAS operation【14CFR_Part39_excerpt】.  

3. **MCAS Software Version 2.0 installation (AD 2024-01-02)** - The latest AD, 2024-01-02, supersedes both 2020-05-11 and 2022-03-07 and mandates installation of MCAS Software v2.0 on all 737-8/9 aircraft. MCAS v2.0 replaces earlier versions (v1.7.3 and earlier) and incorporates improved sensor fusion and fault-tolerance logic. Southwest must update its fleet’s flight-control software, certify the change, and maintain records of the installation to remain airworthy under FAA regulation【8d7605e4-e3b9-4e88-a062-8eb2555f2de2】【14CFR_Part39_excerpt】.  

Thus, Southwest’s full compliance story is: grounding → return-to-service per AD 2020-05-11 → enhanced AOA monitoring per AD 2022-03-07 → MCAS v2.0 installation per AD 2024-01-02, with each step required for continued operation of its 737 MAX fleet.

results.answer: The regulatory chain begins with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issuing an Airworthiness Directive (AD) that applies to the Boeing 737 MAX and its LEAP-1B engines. The most recent directive, **FAA AD 2024-01-02**, supersedes earlier ADs (FAA AD 2020-05-11 and FAA AD 2022-03-07) and mandates inspection of the LEAP-1B engine mount and related structures【6f5d3005-e912-4919-a993-c075ef911dd4】. The directive is incorporated into the aircraft’s maintenance program and is referenced in the **Boeing 737-MAX Maintenance Manual, Chapter 71-21-05 - “CFM LEAP-1B Engine Mount - Inspection and Maintenance”**【701c36fd-2816-44a0-acff-d15e6a205bf0】. The maintenance crew, following the procedures in that chapter, performs the required inspections and any corrective actions in accordance with the FAA AD. The crew’s work is documented and reported back to the airline’s fleet management, which ensures compliance with the FAA’s regulatory requirements.

The FAA’s compliance chain for Southwest Airlines’ 737 MAX fleet begins with the original return-to-service directive, **FAA-AD-2020-05-11** (effective May 27 2020)【Chunk 714da224-4d04-46f9-ae7f-d85ca12a9df5】, which mandated the first set of safety upgrades after the grounding was lifted. In March 2022 the FAA issued **FAA-AD-2022-03-07**【Chunk 25012d55-9a18-499d-992c-741ce79c9555】, superseding the 2020 directive and adding enhanced angle-of-attack (AOA) sensor monitoring for all 737-8/9 aircraft. The most recent directive, **FAA-AD-2024-01-02**【Chunk 85a191d3-fe90-4ca6-bacb-d01fb94b5157], supersedes both earlier ADs and requires installation of MCAS Software v2.0 on all affected 737-8/9 airplanes.  

Southwest Airlines’ fleet, which began operating 737 MAX 8s in 2017 and returned them to revenue service in March 2021【Chunk e7129ab9-123a-4aa4-be4e-808a90f65dac】, is subject to the 2024 AD. The airline’s Fleet Management department must ensure that every 737 MAX in its registry-documented in the 2024 fleet registry【Chunk 09c050d9-0f9b-4d6f-903c-317b35f2852a】-has the MCAS Software v2.0 installed and all earlier requirements satisfied. Thus the compliance chain flows: **FAA-AD-2020-05-11 → FAA-AD-2022-03-07 → FAA-AD-2024-01-02**, culminating in Southwest’s implementation of the MCAS upgrade across its 737 MAX fleet.
